newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOXING-CHAMPION VASQUEZ BREAKS OPPONENT'S JAW.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CHAMPION VASQUEZ BREAKS OPPONENT'S JAW.

text.p: Japan's Yuji Watanabe had his jaw broken in two places as his challenge for Puerto Rican Wilfredo Vasquez's World Boxing Association featherweight crown ended in fifth round defeat on Sunday.
The challenger was floored twice in the second round and again in the fifth before British referee John Coyle stopped the fight.
The end came 31 seconds into the fifth round after the champion stood Watanabe up with a left upper-cut and then landed a devastating right cross.
Watanabe sank to the canvas but as he struggled to regain his feet, the referee stepped in.
From the beginning, Vasquez hammered Watanabe with right hand punches.
The challenger went down in the second after a looping right and again after a sharp left, taking a standing eight count, only to be saved by the bell with Vasquez poised to finish the fight.

Watanabe attempted to rally in the third and fourth rounds, going toe-to-toe with the champion and landing the occasional blow, but it was a brief respite before his third loss in 22 bouts. It was Vasquez's 48th victory.
"I want to defend my title at this weight two more times and then move up and try to win the junior-lightweight championship," Vasquez said.
